business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "Backed by a legacy dating to 1997, Cineline India, through its flagship brand MovieMAX, is building a fast-growing, technology-led cinemas across India, blending premium experiences with accessible entertainment."
- The deck frames the story as "Emerging from a Regional Player to a National Cinema Exhibitor", with a Screen Count Trend slide showing 21 (Apr-22), a Current count of 85, and an Estimated count FY27 of 105-110, tagged "~4x".
- Deck claims "Cineline emerged as the leading movie exhibitor in Q1 FY27, recording the highest growth in admissions, Gross Box Office Collections (GBOC), and combined GBOC + F&B revenues."
- The MovieMAX Edge is stated as curated luxury design and premium F&B, "Advanced 2K & 4K projections paired with immersive 7.1 surround sound", and identifying high-potential hubs (a separate timeline slide cites 4K projection and Dolby Atmos from 2022).

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Fire loss] A P&L footnote records an exceptional item being "a WDV of Fixed assets lost in Fire at Ghaziabad and as required under IND-AS 16. Company has filed a claim with Insurance company and expected to settle in due course of time."
- [Leadership] Mr. Rajeev Sharma has been appointed Joint CEO of Cineline India Limited; he was previously CEO of NY Cinemas (the multiplex chain promoted by Ajay Devgn), later Group CEO at ADF, and spent ~15 years with Fujifilm through PID Pvt. Ltd. as CEO.
- [Promoter group] Promoters are the Kanakia family — Mr. Rasesh B. Kanakia (Chairman, started real estate development in 1986), Mr. Himanshu B. Kanakia (Managing Director) and Mr. Ashish R. Kanakia (Chief Executive Officer).
- [Industry backdrop, Ormax Jan-Jun 2026] Jan-Jun 2026 India box office reached Rs 6,398 Cr, the highest first-half total since the pandemic, exceeding 2025 by nearly Rs 650 Cr; footfalls rose 5% YoY to 37.8 crore, reversing three years of decline.
- [Industry concentration] Rs 100 Cr grossers fell from 17 to 13 and the top 15 films accounted for 58% of revenues (up from 49% in 2025), with Dhurandhar: The Revenge alone contributing 20% of H1 2026 collections — the deck calls this "growing box office concentration among a few blockbuster releases".
